items.q: After years of complaints from tenants, the city council finally voted to ______ the by-law that let landlords evict without notice.
items.vi: Sau nhiều năm bị người thuê nhà phàn nàn, hội đồng thành phố cuối cùng đã bỏ phiếu bãi bỏ quy định cho phép chủ nhà đuổi người thuê mà không cần báo trước.
items.explanation: Word choice: a by-law (a law) is officially cancelled by a vote — repeal = cancel a law. ✗ retract — take back a statement or offer, not a law; ✗ cancel — call off an event, order or booking, not the verb used for legislation; ✗ dismiss — reject a case, idea or employee.

items.q: Having already been cautioned twice for leaking to the press, the junior minister knew he was ______.
items.vi: Đã hai lần bị cảnh cáo vì để lộ tin cho báo chí, vị thứ trưởng trẻ biết mình đang ở thế ngàn cân treo sợi tóc.
items.explanation: Idiom: cautioned twice means one more mistake will finish him — on thin ice = in a risky position. ✗ on the fence — undecided between two sides; ✗ on the rocks — failing (a marriage, a business); ✗ on cloud nine — extremely happy.

items.q: ______ has a single online rumour wiped so much value off a listed company as the one that circulated on Monday.
items.vi: Hiếm khi một tin đồn trên mạng lại làm bốc hơi nhiều giá trị của một công ty niêm yết đến vậy như tin đồn lan truyền hôm thứ Hai.
items.explanation: Inversion after a negative adverb: has a single online rumour wiped (auxiliary before subject) needs a fronted word like Seldom (= rarely). ✗ Not only — needs a matching but (also) clause, which the sentence lacks; ✗ Not until — must be followed by a time clause (Not until Monday did…) before the inverted clause; ✗ Only when — same: needs a clause (Only when it spread did…) first.

items.q: Residents complained that the unlit stairwells had turned the estate into a ______ ground for petty crime.
items.vi: Cư dân than phiền rằng những cầu thang không có đèn đã biến khu chung cư thành mảnh đất màu mỡ cho tội phạm vặt.
items.explanation: Collocation: a place where something bad develops is a breeding ground (for crime, disease, ideas) — clue: unlit stairwells … petty crime. ✗ feeding ground — where animals feed, not where crime develops; ✗ growing ground — not a fixed phrase; ✗ nursing ground — not a fixed phrase (nursing = caring for the sick).

items.q: The commissioner announced that she would ______ at the end of the year rather than face a vote of no confidence.
items.vi: Bà cảnh sát trưởng tuyên bố sẽ từ chức vào cuối năm thay vì đối mặt với cuộc bỏ phiếu bất tín nhiệm.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: rather than face a vote of no confidence means she will leave her post — step down = resign. ✗ step in — intervene to help or take control; ✗ step up — increase (efforts) or take on more responsibility, the opposite here; ✗ stand by — wait ready, or support someone.

items.q: The tribunal recommended that the landlord ______ the deposit in full within fourteen days.
items.vi: Toà án đã khuyến nghị rằng chủ nhà phải hoàn trả toàn bộ tiền đặt cọc trong vòng mười bốn ngày.
items.explanation: Mandative subjunctive: after recommended that (also suggest, insist, demand) the verb is the base form return, whatever the subject or tense. ✗ returns — present -s is an ordinary indicative, not used after a recommendation; ✗ returned — past tense does not follow recommended that; the base form stays even after a past reporting verb; ✗ will return — a future modal is not used in a that-clause of recommendation.

items.q: The Court of Appeal ______ the conviction after DNA evidence showed the defendant had been elsewhere that night.
items.vi: Toà phúc thẩm đã huỷ bản án sau khi bằng chứng ADN cho thấy bị cáo ở nơi khác vào đêm hôm đó.
items.explanation: Word choice: a court declares a conviction invalid — quash = cancel a legal decision. ✗ abolished — ends a law, system or institution, not a single verdict; ✗ suspended — puts a sentence or rule on hold temporarily; the DNA evidence cancels it outright; ✗ terminated — ends a contract or employment.

items.q: The ombudsman insisted that the council ______ its reasons in full, ______ residents assume the decision had been arbitrary.
items.vi: Thanh tra viên yêu cầu hội đồng phải giải thích rõ ràng đầy đủ lý do, kẻo người dân cho rằng quyết định đó là tuỳ tiện.
items.explanation: Double blank: spell out = explain clearly and in detail (its reasons in full); lest = for fear that, followed by a base-form verb (residents assume). ✗ spill out / lest — spill out means pour or flow out, not explain; ✗ spell out / unless — unless (= if not) reverses the logic: the reasons are given so residents will NOT assume; ✗ spill over / so that — spill over means spread beyond a limit, wrong meaning.

items.q: With no way of knowing how many people would turn up to the housing consultation, the planning officers decided to ______.
items.vi: Không thể biết sẽ có bao nhiêu người đến buổi tham vấn về nhà ở, các cán bộ quy hoạch quyết định tuỳ cơ ứng biến.
items.explanation: Idiom: no way of knowing how many people would turn up means they cannot plan — play it by ear = decide as things happen. ✗ play for time — delay deliberately to gain an advantage; ✗ play the field — date many people, not commit to one; ✗ play with fire — take a dangerous risk.

items.q: The defendant ______ been at the scene; his phone records place him fifty miles away at the time.
items.vi: Bị cáo không thể nào có mặt ở hiện trường được; dữ liệu điện thoại cho thấy anh ta ở cách đó năm mươi dặm vào thời điểm đó.
items.explanation: Modal deduction: phone records place him fifty miles away is proof, so can't have + past participle = it is impossible that he was there. ✗ mustn't have — must have deduces that something DID happen; its negative is can't have, not mustn't have; ✗ needn't have — it was unnecessary (but he did it), wrong meaning; ✗ shouldn't have — criticism of something he did, not a deduction.

items.q: The judge ______ a heavy fine on the developer for ignoring the safety order.
items.vi: Thẩm phán đã áp mức phạt nặng lên chủ đầu tư vì phớt lờ lệnh an toàn.
items.explanation: Collocation: a judge imposes a fine/penalty/sentence on someone — clue: a heavy fine on. ✗ inflicted — you inflict pain, damage or a defeat, and it is not the legal verb for a fine; ✗ charged — you charge a fee or a price, or charge someone with a crime; ✗ delivered — you deliver a verdict or a speech, not a fine.

items.q: The housing charity was forced to ______ its night-shelter programme when the council grant ran out.
items.vi: Tổ chức từ thiện về nhà ở buộc phải ngừng chương trình nhà tạm trú ban đêm khi khoản tài trợ của hội đồng cạn kiệt.
items.explanation: Word choice: a programme or service that stops is discontinued. ✗ disband — break up a group of people (a band, a committee); ✗ dissolve — formally end a parliament, marriage or company; ✗ dispel — drive away doubts, fears or myths.

items.q: ______ loudly residents object, the developer has the legal right to proceed once planning permission is granted.
items.vi: Dù người dân phản đối lớn tiếng đến đâu, chủ đầu tư vẫn có quyền hợp pháp tiến hành một khi đã được cấp phép quy hoạch.
items.explanation: Concession: However + adverb (However loudly = no matter how loudly) heads a clause with its own subject and verb (residents object). ✗ Whatever — must be followed by a noun (Whatever objections…), not the adverb loudly; ✗ Although — takes a full clause directly (Although residents object…), it cannot be followed by loudly; ✗ Despite — a preposition, needs a noun phrase or -ing, never a clause.

items.q: Faced with spiralling costs and a hostile audit, the ministry finally decided to ______ the new stadium.
items.vi: Đối mặt với chi phí leo thang và một cuộc kiểm toán bất lợi, bộ cuối cùng quyết định ngừng hẳn dự án sân vận động mới.
items.explanation: Idiom: spiralling costs and a hostile audit lead the ministry to stop funding the project — pull the plug on = end something by withdrawing support. ✗ pull the wool over — deceive someone (…someone's eyes), wrong meaning and incomplete; ✗ pull the strings behind — secretly control something, not stop it; ✗ pull rank on — use your seniority over a person, not a stadium.

items.q: After years of rising rents, many young graduates have been reduced to ______ in converted garages on the edge of town.
items.vi: Sau nhiều năm giá thuê tăng, nhiều cử nhân trẻ đã rơi vào cảnh phải sống trong những gara cải tạo ở rìa thành phố.
items.explanation: Gerund after a preposition: in be reduced to (= be forced into a worse state) the to is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing: reduced to living. ✗ live — a bare infinitive; to here is not the infinitive marker; ✗ be living — same error, an infinitive form after prepositional to; ✗ have lived — a perfect infinitive, also impossible after a preposition.

items.q: Police believe the riots were ______ by a rumour that an officer had shot an unarmed teenager.
items.vi: Cảnh sát tin rằng cuộc bạo loạn đã bị kích động bởi tin đồn rằng một sĩ quan đã bắn một thiếu niên không vũ trang.
items.explanation: Word choice: riots are instigated (= provoked, stirred up) by a rumour. ✗ inaugurated — formally open a building or start a president's term; ✗ instituted — set up a system, policy or procedure; ✗ installed — put equipment in place or put a person into a post.

items.q: ______ orbit, the delta’s patchwork of shrimp farms looks like a sheet of shattered glass.
items.vi: Nhìn từ quỹ đạo, mạng lưới đầm nuôi tôm chằng chịt của vùng châu thổ trông như một tấm kính vỡ.
items.explanation: Reduced clause: the subject the delta’s patchwork of shrimp farms is what is seen, not what sees, so the passive participle is needed: Seen from orbit (= when it is seen from orbit). ✗ Seeing from — active participle would make the shrimp farms the viewer; ✗ To see from — an infinitive states a purpose (in order to see), not a viewpoint; ✗ Having seen from — active and perfect, again makes the farms the viewer.

items.q: The minister's resignation came ______ the ______, catching even his closest aides unawares.
items.vi: Việc bộ trưởng từ chức diễn ra hoàn toàn bất ngờ, khiến ngay cả các trợ lý thân cận nhất của ông cũng trở tay không kịp.
items.explanation: Double blank: catching even his closest aides unawares means the resignation was unexpected — came out of the blue = happened without warning. ✗ off / cuff — off the cuff = without preparation (a remark, a speech), not a sudden event; ✗ under / radar — under the radar = unnoticed, but the resignation was noticed, just unexpected; ✗ out of / ordinary — out of the ordinary = unusual, an adjective phrase that does not go with came.

items.q: It is high time the government ______ something about the chronic shortage of social housing.
items.vi: Đã đến lúc chính phủ phải làm gì đó về tình trạng thiếu nhà ở xã hội kinh niên.
items.explanation: Past subjunctive: It is high time + past form means the action is overdue but refers to now: the government did. ✗ does — present tense is not used after it's (high) time; ✗ do — the base subjunctive belongs after suggest/insist that, not after it's time; ✗ will do — a future form is not used in this pattern.

items.q: The new chief constable has vowed to ______ bribery in the traffic division once and for all.
items.vi: Tân cảnh sát trưởng đã thề sẽ dẹp tận gốc nạn hối lộ trong đội cảnh sát giao thông một lần và mãi mãi.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: bribery … once and for all means getting rid of it completely — stamp out = eliminate something bad. ✗ rule out — exclude a possibility or option; ✗ wear out — make something exhausted or worn by use; ✗ phase out — withdraw gradually in stages, which clashes with once and for all.

items.q: ______ tenants had even heard of the compensation scheme, so turnout at the meeting was poor.
items.vi: Rất ít người thuê nhà từng nghe nói đến chương trình bồi thường, nên số người đến dự họp rất thưa thớt.
items.explanation: Quantifier: tenants is a plural countable noun and turnout … was poor shows a negative sense, so Few (= hardly any). ✗ A few — positive (= some, enough), which would not explain a poor turnout; ✗ Little — used only with uncountable nouns (little money); ✗ A little — uncountable and positive, doubly wrong.

items.q: Economists warned the city not to ______ by tying its entire budget to tourism revenue.
options: put the cart before the horse
put all its eggs in one basket
count its chickens before they hatch
items.answer: put all its eggs in one basket
items.vi: Các nhà kinh tế cảnh báo thành phố không nên dồn hết trứng vào một giỏ bằng cách gắn toàn bộ ngân sách vào nguồn thu từ du lịch.
items.explanation: Idiom: tying its entire budget to tourism revenue = relying on one source — put all its eggs in one basket = depend entirely on one thing. ✗ put the cart before the horse — do things in the wrong order; ✗ walk on eggshells — act very carefully to avoid upsetting someone; ✗ count its chickens before they hatch — assume success before it is certain.

items.q: Only after the third burglary in a single month ______ to install cameras on the estate.
items.vi: Chỉ sau vụ trộm thứ ba trong vòng một tháng, hội đồng mới đồng ý lắp camera trong khu chung cư.
items.explanation: Inversion: a fronted Only after + phrase forces the auxiliary before the subject in the main clause: did the council agree. ✗ the council agreed — normal order, no inversion; ✗ the council did agree — the auxiliary did must come BEFORE the council, not after; ✗ the council had agreed — no inversion, and the past perfect needs an earlier event to precede, which the sentence does not give.

items.q: The licensing board ______ the nightclub's licence after a third stabbing on its premises in a year.
items.vi: Ban cấp phép đã thu hồi giấy phép của hộp đêm sau vụ đâm chém thứ ba trong khuôn viên trong vòng một năm.
items.explanation: Word choice: a licence or permit is officially withdrawn — revoke = cancel an official permission. ✗ refuted — prove a claim or argument false; ✗ retrieved — get something back that was lost or left somewhere; ✗ repelled — drive away an attack or an enemy.

items.q: Prosecutors ______ doubt on the alibi after CCTV placed the defendant near the scene an hour before the robbery.
items.vi: Các công tố viên đã gieo nghi ngờ lên bằng chứng ngoại phạm sau khi camera an ninh cho thấy bị cáo ở gần hiện trường một giờ trước vụ cướp.
items.explanation: Collocation: cast doubt on something = make people question it — clue: doubt on the alibi. ✗ placed — you place trust/emphasis on, not doubt; ✗ laid — you lay blame on someone, not doubt; ✗ set — you set a date or a record; it does not combine with doubt.
